§1 — Warm-Up · Hot Take
True or False — About You
S-B starts with production — no looking at notes · Activate S1A vocabulary from memory · Speed matters
⏱ 5–8 MIN
Can you…?
I'd like…
I need…
I like…
⚡ No notes allowed. Your teacher says a sentence. You say TRUE (it's correct English) or FALSE (it has an error). Be fast — first hand up wins the point.

1. "She can to drive a truck." ❓
2. "I need a pen — do you have one?" ❓
3. "Can I have a coffee, please?" ❓
4. "I like drinking water at my desk." ❓
5. "I don't like tea — I prefer coffee." ❓
💬 Partner drill — 45 seconds: Say 3 TRUE sentences about yourself using words from last session. Partner listens and gives thumbs up ✅ or thumbs down ❌. No Spanish. Go!
⚡ Teacher note: Answers: 1=FALSE (can't use "to"), 2=TRUE, 3=TRUE, 4=FALSE (like+gerund not A1.1), 5=TRUE. Run quickly — 2 min max. This is an error radar, not a teaching moment. Note who gets #1 and #4 wrong — those are the priority corrections for today. Then move to §2 immediately.
⚡ Quick Win — 20 seconds

No notes. No thinking. Just say it: "I can [one real skill]. I need [one thing right now]. I like [one thing about your job]." Three sentences. Boom. That's the whole module in 10 words.

Teacher Note — Running §1 in S1B

S1B never re-teaches. It reveals. The warm-up exposes who retained S1A and who needs a push. Say: "Today we don't learn — we USE. Everything from last session, but faster, longer, and with real people." Energy level: higher than S1A from minute one.

§2 — Speaking Topic · Pitch & Debate Round
Sell Your Skills — Who's the Best Hire?
Production round · Free output · Real job context · can/like/need in connected speech
⏱ 8–10 MIN
Teacher Note — Pitch Round Setup

Tell the class: "You are all applying for the same job at a new company in Celaya. The job is: Operations Coordinator. You have 60 seconds to sell yourself. Use: I can [skill], I can't [limitation], I like [relevant thing], I need [one thing to do the job well]." Set the timer. No notes allowed in Round 2 or 3. This is the core production moment of S1B.

🎤
Round 1 — Pitch
Each student has 60 seconds to present their skills to the "hiring manager" (teacher). Must use: 2 × can, 1 × can't, 1 × like, 1 × need. No notes.
⚔️
Round 2 — Debate
Teacher picks the "top 2 candidates." They each make their best case in 30 seconds. Class votes: whose English was most natural? Most correct? Most confident?
🔄
Round 3 — Relay
Student A makes 1 "can" statement. Student B responds with "can you also [skill]?" Student A answers. Then B adds their own. Chain grows until someone repeats or pauses 3+ seconds.
Model Pitch — Ana García
Listen to this model answer. What structures does Ana use? Count the "can" sentences. How many "like" and "need" sentences do you hear?

"Hi. My name is Ana García. I'm a coordinator. I can use Excel and SAP very well — I use them every day. I can also manage a team and I can communicate with clients in English. I can't design graphics — that's not my skill. But I like problem-solving and I like teamwork. I need a laptop and a fast internet connection to do my job well. I think I'm a good candidate."
Structures used: 4 × can, 1 × can't, 2 × like, 1 × need. Note: "communicate with clients" — professional colocation A1.1 students can use immediately.

Teacher Note — Error Correction Protocol

During pitches, write errors on the board WITHOUT stopping the student. After each pitch: "Good job. Two things to fix: [error 1] → [correction]. [error 2] → [correction]." Keep corrections to max 2 per student. Students repeat the corrected sentence once. Move on. Speed and confidence matter more than perfection at this stage.

§3 — Vocabulary · Speed Round
12 Words — No Hesitation
Fluency over accuracy now · Click cards for instant context sentences · Relay game for production
⏱ 8–10 MIN
Teacher Note — Speed Round Rules

Project cards on screen. Teacher taps a card — class must say 1 sentence using that word IMMEDIATELY. No pause longer than 3 seconds. Wrong structure → class calls "ERROR!" and someone fixes it. Right structure → class says "CORRECT!" and moves on. The goal: zero hesitation time from word → sentence. This trains automaticity — the A1.1 fluency target.

speak
Can you speak…?
"I can speak English and a little French." · "Can you speak slowly, please?"
drive
I can / I can't…
"I can drive — I have my licence." · "She can't drive — she uses the metro."
use Excel
Can you use…?
"Yes, I can use Excel — I make reports every day." · "Can you use Excel? — No, but I can learn."
manage
She can manage…
"She can manage a team of 8 people." · "I can't manage the whole project alone."
help
Can you help me…?
"Can you help me with this form?" · "Sure! I can help you — no problem."
design
He can design…
"He can design the presentation slides." · "I can't design — I need a graphic designer."
coffee
Can I have…?
"Can I have a coffee, please?" · "I like coffee — I drink it every morning."
sandwich
I'd like a…
"I'd like a sandwich and a water, please." · "Can I get a sandwich? — Sure, anything else?"
water
I need…
"I need water — I'm very thirsty." · "Can I have some water, please?"
pen
I need a pen…
"I need a pen — do you have one?" · "Can I borrow your pen? — Sure, no problem."
charger
Can I borrow…?
"Can I borrow your charger? Mine is at home." · "I need a charger — my phone is at 2%."
notebook
I want a new…
"I want a new notebook for the meeting." · "I need a notebook — can you give me one?"
🗣️ Relay Game: Student A picks any card and says a sentence. Student B continues with the NEXT card. Round the class. No repeating a card. No stopping. If someone stops for 3+ seconds → sit down. Last student standing wins.
Teacher Note — Speed Round Badge

When the full relay is completed without stopping (all 12 cards), award badge b1 to the class collectively. If they don't complete it, do it a second time — and give the badge when they succeed. The goal is fluency under time pressure, not perfection.

§4 — Colloquial · Review & Production
4 Phrases — No Script
From S1A phrases to real conversation · Role-play drill · Natural speed · No translation
⏱ 5 MIN
Teacher Note — Colloquial Drill Format

Rapid-fire role play pairs. Teacher calls: "CAFETERIA" → pairs do the ordering role-play. "HELP REQUEST" → A asks "Can you help me?" B responds "Sure, no problem!" and invents a helpful action. "DECLINE" → A offers something, B uses "I'm not really into [it]." Clock it: 30 seconds per scenario. Switch roles. The goal: these 4 phrases come out without thinking. Zero translation time.

Drill A — Cafeteria Counter (S-S · 45 sec)
A = cafeteria worker. B = customer. B orders 2 things using "Can I get…?" and "I'd like…" A responds with "Anything else?" B closes with "That's all, thanks!" Switch roles. Do it TWICE — faster the second time.
💡 B: "Can I get a coffee, please? And I'd like a sandwich." A: "Sure! Anything else?" B: "No, that's all, thanks!"
Drill B — Help Request Chain (Class · 60 sec)
A asks B: "Can you help me with [task]?" B says "Sure, no problem!" and invents what they do to help. B then turns to C with a NEW help request. Chain around the room. No repeating the same task twice.
💡 A: "Can you help me with the report?" B: "Sure, no problem! I can check the numbers." [B→C]: "Can you help me with the presentation?" C: "Sure, no problem! I can design the slides."
Drill C — Polite Decline (S-S · 30 sec each)
A offers something: food, a task, a social invite. B declines politely using "I'm not really into [it]" and suggests an alternative. Then switch. Be creative — the more unexpected the offer, the more fun and memorable.
💡 A: "Do you want tea?" B: "I'm not really into tea — but can I get a coffee?" A: "Do you want to give the presentation?" B: "I'm not really into public speaking — can you help me with the slides instead?"
Teacher Note — Colloquial Badge

Award badge b2 after Drill C. All three drills = all four phrases in active production. Students who complete all three with zero Spanish earn a mental note — they are your S5 exit task leaders.

§5 — Grammar · Unjumble + Solo Challenge
Build the Sentence — Get It Right
Production accuracy check · can/like/need word order · Error correction in pairs · Solo written challenge
⏱ 10–12 MIN
Teacher Note — Unjumble Pedagogy

Unjumble reveals word-order errors that oral production hides. A student might SAY a correct sentence but BUILD it incorrectly because they've memorized a chunk. This activity separates fluency from accuracy. Run individually (30 sec per sentence) then compare with partner. Teacher: any sentence where 3+ students get it wrong → brief board explanation, then move on.

🎮 Unjumble — Build the Correct Sentence
Score: 0 / 5
Sentence 1 of 5
✏️ Solo Written Challenge — Error Correction
Teacher Note — Error Correction Activity

Students do this individually in writing first (2 min). Then compare with partner. Then class discussion. The errors are ones real A1.1 students make — collected from real classroom observation. Every sentence looks "almost right" to trick students who are guessing rather than thinking.

1. "She can to manage the project." — What's the error?
2. "I like drinking coffee every morning." — Why is this wrong at A1.1?
3. "He need a new charger for his laptop." — Fix it.
4. "Can I to have a water, please?" — What's wrong?
5. "Yes, I can. I can use Excel and design." — Is this correct?
🗣️ Pair check: Take any 2 sentences from the activity and say the CORRECT version out loud to your partner. Then make a new sentence using the same structure — about your real job.
§6 — Listening · Assessment Round
Cafeteria Conversation — Real Life Audio
Listening with higher focus · No script first time · Comprehension + True/False · Leaderboard scoring
⏱ 8–10 MIN
Teacher Note — S1B Listening Protocol

Play the script FIRST without revealing it. Students listen and answer questions from memory. THEN reveal the script for the second listen. In S1A, they had the script available — in S1B they work from listening only on the first pass. This is a significant jump in listening demand and mimics real-world English use. After questions, reveal script and compare their answers.

Skills & Actions Monologue — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M5 · S1B · Voice: Lauren (ElevenLabs) · Real Audio
0:00 --:--
⚡ First listen: Close notes. Listen only — what CAN Ana do? What does she NEED? What does she LIKE? Answer from memory, then open script.
Hi! My name is Ana García. I'm a coordinator at Vertex Logistics in Celaya. Today I want to talk about my work skills.

At my job, I can use Excel every day — I organize schedules and write reports. I can also manage a small team. Right now I manage four people and I like it. I can speak English too — not perfect, but I can communicate with our US clients. I can drive, so I visit our suppliers in Querétaro when I need to.

But I can't design graphics — I'm not a designer. And I can't speak French.

What do I like? I like my team — they are friendly. I like my schedule: I start at eight and finish at five. What do I need? I need a good laptop, a notebook for meetings, and coffee. A lot of coffee! Can I get one now? Sure, no problem!
📎 A1.1 · M5 · S1B · ~160 words · Voice: Lauren (ElevenLabs) · Speed: 0.78 · Monologue: Ana García — Skills & Needs
✏️ Comprehension — Multiple Choice
1. Name TWO things Ana can do at work.
2. What does Ana NEED to do her job well?
✏️ True or False
Ana can speak French — she uses it with international clients.
Ana likes her team — she says they are friendly and helpful.
Ana uses a notebook to write things down in meetings.
Ana manages a team of four people at Vertex Logistics.

§7 — Production · Spin the Wheel + Solo Challenge
Speak — No Excuses
Spin the Wheel speaking prompts · 90-sec Solo Challenge · Timer · Rubric · Badge b4
⏱ 12–15 MIN
"English is useful for my real job RIGHT NOW — not just in the future."
Disagree50 / 50Agree
50%
Teacher Note — Opinion Meter in S1B

After voting, ask: "Who said Agree? Give me ONE example of English you used at work this week — or could use." Students answer with can/need/like sentences. This is covert fluency practice — they think it's a discussion but they're producing the module grammar. High-value 3-minute activity.

🎡 Spin the Wheel — Speaking Prompts
Spin → get a prompt → speak for 30–60 seconds. No notes. No Spanish. Go!
▼
Your Speaking Prompt
Teacher Note — Wheel Segments

8 segments: each is a different production scenario. After each spin, start the 30-second timer immediately. Student speaks — class listens for errors. Two quick corrections max after each spin. Award badge b3 after 6+ successful spins across the class (not all by the same student).

⭐ Solo Challenge — 90-Second Skills Presentation
Your Final Challenge for This Session
Prepare and give a 90-second presentation to the class (or to your teacher). No notes. No Spanish. Include ALL of the following:

① 3 things you CAN do at work
② 1 thing you CAN'T do
③ 1 thing you LIKE about your job
④ 1 thing you NEED every day
⑤ 1 food or drink you'd like right now (use "Can I get…?" or "I'd like…")
Used 3+ "can" sentences correctly — no "can to"
Used "like" with a noun — not a gerund
Used "need" correctly — 3rd person -s if needed
Used at least 1 colloquial phrase naturally
Spoke for at least 60 seconds without stopping
Earn badge b4 when you complete your solo challenge. Rub­ric checked by teacher. Badge awarded on completion.

✅ I Can Now… — Click each one when confident
I can speak about my work skills for 60+ seconds without stopping — in English, no Spanish
I can order food and drinks naturally: "Can I get a coffee?" / "I'd like a sandwich, please."
I can respond naturally: "Sure, no problem!" / "I'm not really into it." / "That's all, thanks!"
I can catch my own errors: "can to speak" → "can speak" / "like drinking" → "like coffee"
I can talk about what I like, need and want — with nouns only — fast and naturally
🎯 3 Phrases You Will Use This Week — Starting Tomorrow
PHRASE 1
"Can I get a [coffee], please?"
Tomorrow morning, at the cafeteria or in a meeting: use this instead of "I want." One small change. Completely natural. People WILL notice the difference.
PHRASE 2
"Sure, no problem!"
Every time a colleague or client asks you something in English this week: say this. Confident. Positive. Professional. Zero thinking required — that's the goal.
PHRASE 3
"I can [skill] and I can [skill]."
At your next meeting, team standup, or intro with a new colleague: use your real skills in English. "I can manage the schedule and I can use SAP." Done. That's professional English.
